AgentSlang: a language shaped for the agents that write it.

AgentSlang (ASL) is a programming language, a data notation and a set of first-party packages for coding agents. Delimiters, arity and symbols are checked before anything runs, lookups return Option and fallible calls return Result, and the asl toolbelt reads and edits a repository by symbol.

$curl -fsSL https://aslang.dev/install.sh | sh

Preview · not released. The script has not been verified on a clean machine yet: status in the docs

$asl '(:tools)'

Once installed, this lists every toolbelt operation.

01Why AgentSlang

Three places model-written code goes wrong.

Mainstream languages were designed for a person at a keyboard. ASL is built around three kinds of mistake that a checker or a tool can catch before they cost a run.

01 · Structure

Syntax and symbol errors stop before the run

asl check verifies delimiter balance, arity and symbol resolution before anything executes. A truncated form is rejected with ERR_UNBALANCED, an invented name with ERR_UNKNOWN_SYMBOL.

asl check · ERR_UNBALANCED · ERR_UNKNOWN_SYMBOL
02 · Semantics

No nil and no exceptions

The standard lookups (listHead, listGet, stringSlice, mapGet) return (some v) or (none); fallible builtins return (ok v) or (err e), taken apart with match. Integer overflow and division by zero trap.

Option · Result · match
03 · Context

Read by symbol, edit by exact text

The asl toolbelt returns one definition with its line range instead of a whole file, stages exact replacements in a session buffer outside the working tree, and writes each file atomically on flush.

(:read :symbol) · (:edit) · (:flush)
02Token cost

One tool call: 51, 30 or 18 tokens.

The same git status call, counted with cl100k_base. A positional frame does not repeat key names on every call. This is one example, not a benchmark: a positional JSON array of the same fields counts 17 tokens.

Language design

Small, predictable, machine-legible

Positional enums with match, immutable record updates via with, ! effect marks as a convention, and camelCase builtins.

enums & matchrecords & with! markscamelCase

Checks, contracts and process control

asl check and asl test, contract checks, process helpers and session replay.

04The toolbelt

One call, several operations, one flush.

Inside a git repository an agent queries symbols, reads exact definitions, stages edits, checks them and writes them, several forms to a call.

  1. asl '(:query :text "handleRequest")'Find the definitions and uses of a symbol in code, with a count of mentions elsewhere.
  2. asl '(:read :file "src/server.asl" :symbol "handleRequest")'Read one function with its line range instead of the whole file.
  3. asl '(:edit :file "src/server.asl" :old "…" :new "…")'Stage an exact replacement; the receipt says whether the file still parses.
  4. asl '(:diff) (:check :file "src/server.asl")'Inspect the staged change and run the checker in one call.
  5. asl '(:flush)'Write the staged edits, each file atomically, or (:discard) to drop them.
05Under the hood

Language rules and compile targets.

Each rule removes a class of ambiguity. Checked programs lower to LLVM IR for native code and WebAssembly, and to JavaScript, Python and Go.

Structure you can count

Every ( [ and { pairs with its own closing bracket. A truncated form is rejected with ERR_UNBALANCED before anything runs.

ERR_UNBALANCED: unclosed (

Failures are values

Standard lookups return (some v) or (none) and fallible calls return (ok v) or (err e), unwrapped with match, optionOr or resultOr.

(match (mapGet users id) ((some u) u.name) ((none) "guest"))

Docs live as data

Documentation lives as (:doc :symbol ... :text ...) rows in doc.asn rather than prose comments inside source files.

(:doc :symbol "app/http#serve" :text "...")

Compile targets

asl-target-llvm emits native code through clang and wasm32 modules such as this page; the target is still marked partial. asl-target-js emits an ES module with .d.mts types, and the Python and Go targets pass their fixtures.

asl-target-llvm · wasm32 · js · py · go
